# Draft:Tony Shaw (historian)

Tony shaw wikitext · TXT
Copy
Tony Shaw is a British historian and Professor of Contemporary History at the University of Hertfordshire. He specialises in the history of film, international propaganda, and the Cold War, and is the author of six books, four edited volumes, and numerous research articles.
Shaw was educated at the University of Leeds and the University of Oxford. Since 2001 he has been a Fellow of the Royal Historical Society. He has held an Associate Fellowship at Oxford's Rothermere American Institute and at the LSE IDEAS Cold War Studies Programme, and has served as a Visiting Professor at the University of Southern California in Los Angeles.
Shaw has been based at the University of Hertfordshire since the early 2000s. He is co-editor of the journal Contemporary British History and serves on the editorial board of American Communist History. He has acted as a historical consultant for television and radio productions in the United Kingdom, the United States, and Canada.
His most widely cited monograph, ''Hollywood's Cold War (2007), was reviewed in the American Historical Review, the Journal of Cold War Studies, The Historian, and CHOICE'', the last of which described it as "important for political and cultural history" and "highly recommended". Shaw's work ranges from the Suez Crisis and McCarthyism to the history of terrorism on film and the relationship between Hollywood and Israel.
Research
Shaw's research centres on the intersection of cinema, propaganda, and twentieth-century international history. His work draws extensively on declassified government documents, studio archives, and filmmakers' private papers. He has written on McCarthyism, the Suez Crisis, Cold War cultural diplomacy, the history of terrorism on screen, and the modern history of the Middle East.
''Hollywood's Cold War'' (2007) provided the first comprehensive account of Hollywood's propaganda role during the Cold War, tracing the relationship between filmmakers, censors, politicians, and government propagandists from the 1917 Bolshevik Revolution to the fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989. A companion volume co-authored with Denise J. Youngblood, Cinematic Cold War: The American and Soviet Struggle for Hearts and Minds (University Press of Kansas, 2010), broadened the analysis to encompass Soviet cinema alongside Hollywood's output.
Cinematic Terror: A Global History of Terrorism on Film (Bloomsbury, 2015) extended Shaw's enquiry to the international history of terrorism as depicted on screen.
Shaw co-authored Hollywood and Israel: A History (Columbia University Press, 2022) with Giora Goodman of Kinneret College. Drawing on American and Israeli archives, studio records, and interviews, the book chronicles the relationship between the Hollywood entertainment industry and Israel from the 1940s to the present, examining the roles of figures including Frank Sinatra, Barbra Streisand, Vanessa Redgrave, and Steven Spielberg.
Shaw is currently working on two further projects: an international history of football during the Cold War, to be published by Cambridge University Press, and a study of the British Foreign Office's Cold War clandestine propaganda agency, the Information Research Department.
